summary: Friedemann Friese's ancient-Egypt entry in his oasis series is a deck/bag-building worker-placement game where players expand canals and fields on a hex-grid personal board while managing a growing pool of action cards. It rewards long-term engine planning as much as tactical adaptation, with a fair bit of solitaire-style optimization on your own tableau.
praised: satisfying engine-building progression as your deck of actions grows
good solo mode and scales well
criticised: can run long and feel a bit dry or fiddly with bookkeeping
interaction is fairly limited, mostly a multiplayer solitaire experience
learning curve to see how all the systems interlock

interaction.kind: shared market/resource competition, mostly parallel play

scoring.why: final score combines developed land, buildings, and goods produced, favoring whoever built the most efficient personal engine

similar: Faiyum: The Rise of Egypt expansions
